items.text: Siku moja buibui Anansi alivuna viazi vikuu shambani mwake. Vilipendeza na kuonekana vitamu sana. Alivichoma taratibu kwenye moto na akaanza kula.

translation_en.text:
One day, Anansi the spider picked
some yams from his garden.
They were extra beautiful delicious
yams, so he baked them carefully in
the fire.
Then he sat down to eat them up.

items.text: Siku moja, Nyame aliamua kumpa Anansi chungu hicho cha hekima. Kila Anansi alipotazama ndani ya chungu cha udongo, alijifunza jambo jipya. Alifurahi sana!

translation_en.text:
One day, Nyame decided that
he would give the pot of
wisdom to Anansi.
Every time Anansi looked in the
clay pot, he learned something
new. It was so exciting!

items.text: Nilisikiliza kwa makini aliponielezea ingawa sikuelewa kwa nini hakumpata mtoto akiwa nyumbani. Alipomaliza kunielezea, nilimuuliza, “Je, ataendelea kunipenda hata baada ya kurudi na mtoto mwingine?”

translation_en.text:
I listened keenly to him as he explained although I didn't
quite understand why she wasn't having the baby at home.
When dad finished explaining, I asked, "Will she still love
me when she comes back with the other baby?"

items.text: Nilimwuliza mjomba iwapo Coco alizaliwa pekee yake. Mjomba alisema kwamba alikuwa na ndugu yake aliyemfanana kabisa. Nilienda kumuona ndugu yake Coco.

translation_en.text:
I asked my uncle if Coco was born alone.
My uncle said that there was another puppy,
exactly like Coco.
I went to see Coco's brother.

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0016_rafiki-yangu-coco.md p3; Text: Ursula Nafula; Illustration: Ursula Nafula; Translation: Ursula Nafula

claims.locator: raw/asp/sw/0016_rafiki-yangu-coco.md p3; Text: Ursula Nafula; Illustration: Ursula Nafula; Translation: Ursula Nafula

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Miezi michache baadaye, Coco na nduguye walikuwa wamekuwa wakubwa. Walikuwa wenye nguvu na wenye afya. Nami singeweza kuwachunga pekee yangu tena.

translation_en.text:
A few months later, Coco and
his brother were big, strong and
healthy.
They were too big for me to
look after on my own.

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0016_rafiki-yangu-coco.md p6; Text: Ursula Nafula; Illustration: Ursula Nafula; Translation: Ursula Nafula

claims.locator: raw/asp/sw/0016_rafiki-yangu-coco.md p6; Text: Ursula Nafula; Illustration: Ursula Nafula; Translation: Ursula Nafula

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Kwa hivyo nilimuuliza mjombangu kumrudisha nduguye Coco kwake. Lakini Coco alipoachwa pekee yake, alihuzunika mno. Ilionekana kana kwamba aliniuliza, “Kwa nini ulifanya hivyo?”

translation_en.text:
So I asked my uncle to take
back Coco's brother.
But when Coco was left alone,
he looked very sad.
It felt as if he was asking me,
"Why did you do that?"

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0016_rafiki-yangu-coco.md p7; Text: Ursula Nafula; Illustration: Ursula Nafula; Translation: Ursula Nafula

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Nilifurahi sana hadi sikujua nimkumbatie nani kwanza, Coco au mjombangu. Nilijua kwamba Coco angerejelea ile hali yake ya kwaida kwa vile nduguye alikuwa amerudi. Tungeenda kukimbia wanjani tena!

translation_en.text:
I was so happy that I did not
know who to hug first, Coco or
my uncle.
I knew Coco would go back to
his old self now that his brother
was back.
We would go running in the
fields again!

translation_en.text:
The bus was very full, so I had to sit
on my mother's lap.
Tired from the heat and excitement,
I slept the whole way and saw
nothing.

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Kati ya matunda yote katika kibanda, nilipenda tofaa zaidi. Nilipenda umbo na rangi yao. Niliwazia utamu ukoje. Nilimgeukia mama nikamwomba, “mama tafadhali ninunulie moja?”

translation_en.text:
Of all the fruits at the stall, I liked
the apples most. I liked their shape
and colour. I wondered how they
tasted.
I turned to mother and said, "Could
you buy one for me?"

items.text: Muda mfupi baadaye, mwanamke mmoja alinishika mkono akaniongoza mahali ambapo watoto wengine walikuwepo. Mwanamume mkubwa mwenye mandevu aliniuliza, “jina lako ni nani mwanangu?” Nikamjibu nikilia, “E-ta-bo.”

translation_en.text:
A while later, a woman took me by
the hand and led me to a place
where there were other children.
A big man with a thick beard asked,
"What's your name, boy?"
"E-ta-bo," I replied through my
tears.

translation_en.text:
They had walked for quite a while
but could not find anywhere to build
their new house.
When it became dark, they decided
to climb up a tree and sleep.

items.text: Na hivyo, hawakuafikiana. Kisha mmoja alipiga kelele, “Yule atakayeruka juu zaidi atakuwa mfalme.” “Ndiyo, ndiyo,” walipiga kelele, na wote wakaruka juu, juu angani.

translation_en.text: And so they didn't get very far. Then one bird had an idea. "He who can fly the highest will be king," he said. "Yes, yes," they shouted, and they all flew up, up, into the sky.

translation_en.text: But out from under his wing crept the tiny bird. "Tink, tink! Tink, tink! It is I, the smallest one! I am your king." Vulture was too exhausted to fly any further.

translation_en.text: So down he sailed - with the little bird still under his wing. The other birds were furious with Ncede. They waited for him, ready to pluck out all his feathers.

translation_en.text:
At the bottom of this pool were
two snakes.
One had thick strongly
patterned coils, and the other
was smaller and more delicate.

items.text: “Hatuwezi kuendelea kuishi kwenye dimbwi hili lenye giza na baridi,” waliambiana. “Twende kule juu tukaione ardhi.” “Tutawezaje kuishi kwenye ardhi?” yule nyoka mdogo aliuliza. “Je, tutatambaa kwa matumbo?”

translation_en.text:
"We cannot stay in this dark cold pool any longer," they said to each other.
"Let us go up and see the earth above."
"How will we live on earth?" said the smaller snake.
"Will we crawl on our bellies?"

translation_en.text:
"The birds of the air will not laugh at us for
being so low," said her friend.
"We will not crawl, we will walk!"
Very slowly the snakes uncoiled themselves.
Close together they began to swim up, up, to
the light above.

translation_en.text:

From just beneath their heads grew two arms
with hands and fingers.

translation_en.text:
"We will make our home in the
hills," said Woman. "Each
morning we will see the sun rise
and feel it warm on our backs."
"We will look after the grass
and the trees," said Man. "And
be friends with Bird and Beast."

The machines were first spotted by
the mole family. To be more exact,
by Mister Popples, the eldest who

told the youngest, Little Popples.

grandmother's manyatta, but
she did not get there.
She got lost in the hills.
Akai was afraid.

translation_en.text:
This is how the dream went:
She was lying on her special
mat.
A woman who looked like her
grandmother was watching over
her.
The lady smiled and gave her a
big bowl of camel milk.
Just when Akai stretched out
her hand to take the milk, she
woke up.

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Watu wote wa familia ya Akai waliimba na kucheza kumkaribisha nyumbani. Walimchinja mbuzi, wakachoma nyama na kusherehekea kurudi salama kwa mtoto wao.

translation_en.text:
Akai's family sang and danced
to welcome her home.
They slaughtered a goat,
roasted the meat and
celebrated their child's safe
return.

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Mwanaume yeyote aliyetaka kumwoa Nangila, alilazimika kuleta miti-shamba kutoka ziwa lililokuwa karibu. Dawa hii ingeponya donda alilokuwa nalo bababke Nangila. Ziwa hilo lilijaa mizimu hatari.

translation_en.text:
Anyone who wanted to marry Nangila would have to get a herb from a lake near the village.

This herb would heal her father's wound.

But the lake was filled with dangerous spirits.

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0062_ujasiri-wa-nangila.md p4; Text: Violet Otieno; Illustration: Vusi Malindi; Translation: Ursula Nafula

claims.locator: raw/asp/sw/0062_ujasiri-wa-nangila.md p4; Text: Violet Otieno; Illustration: Vusi Malindi; Translation: Ursula Nafula

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Nangila alijawa na wasiwasi kaka zake pia waliposhindwa kwenda ziwani. Nangila aliamua kwenda mwenyewe ziwani. Mamake alimwambia, "Mwanangu, ikiwa wanaume wenye nguvu wameshindwa, utafaulu?" Nangila hakubadili nia.

translation_en.text:
Nangila felt worried. Not even her brothers would go to the lake. She decided to fetch the herb herself.

Her mother said, "My daughter, if strong men have failed, will you succeed?" But Nangila had made up her mind.

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0062_ujasiri-wa-nangila.md p6; Text: Violet Otieno; Illustration: Vusi Malindi; Translation: Ursula Nafula

claims.locator: raw/asp/sw/0062_ujasiri-wa-nangila.md p6; Text: Violet Otieno; Illustration: Vusi Malindi; Translation: Ursula Nafula

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Njiani, Nangila alimsaidia bi kizee mmoja kubeba kuni. Bi kizee alimshukuru, akamwambia, "Nitakueleza jinsi utakavyofika kwenye ziwa la mizimu na namna utakavyofanya."

translation_en.text:
On the way to the lake, Nangila met an old woman carrying wood. She helped the woman to carry her firewood.

The old woman was grateful. She said to Nangila, "I will tell you how to reach the spirit lake and what to do when you get there."

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0062_ujasiri-wa-nangila.md p7; Text: Violet Otieno; Illustration: Vusi Malindi; Translation: Ursula Nafula

claims.locator: raw/asp/sw/0062_ujasiri-wa-nangila.md p7; Text: Violet Otieno; Illustration: Vusi Malindi; Translation: Ursula Nafula

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Nangila alipofika ufuoni mwa ziwa, aliiona familia ya mizimu ikinywa na kusherehekea. Alisubiri na kutazama. Moja baada ya nyingine, mizimu ilipatwa na usingizi.

translation_en.text:
When she reached the shore of the lake, Nangila saw the spirit family drinking and dancing.

She waited and watched. One by one, the spirits fell asleep.

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0062_ujasiri-wa-nangila.md p8; Text: Violet Otieno; Illustration: Vusi Malindi; Translation: Ursula Nafula

claims.locator: raw/asp/sw/0062_ujasiri-wa-nangila.md p8; Text: Violet Otieno; Illustration: Vusi Malindi; Translation: Ursula Nafula

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Sauti ya Nangila ilikuwa tamu sana hata mizimu ikamtaka aimbe zaidi. Kuimba kwake kulipoifanya ilale tena, Nangila alikimbia haraka akafika kijijini.

translation_en.text:
Nangila's voice was so sweet that the spirits asked her to sing for them again and again.

Her singing sent the spirits back to sleep.

Then Nangila ran very fast until she got to her village.

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0062_ujasiri-wa-nangila.md p11; Text: Violet Otieno; Illustration: Vusi Malindi; Translation: Ursula Nafula

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Baada ya mchezo, tulienda dukani lakini hatukuwa na pesa. Nilianza kulia. Chuma alinikemea, “Acha kulia. Ni wewe ulitaka tucheze kabla ya kwenda dukani.”

translation_en.text:
After the game, we
went to the shop but we
had lost the money.
I started to cry.
Chuma said, "Stop
crying. You wanted us
to play before going to
the shop."

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Kwa hivyo wakati watoto wa Gingile wanaposikia hadithi ya Ngede, wanamheshimu yule ndege. Kila wanapotoa asali, huhakikisha kwamba wanamwachia Kiongozi fungu kubwa!

translation_en.text: And so, when the children of Gingile hear the story of Ngede they have respect for the little bird. Whenever they harvest honey, they make sure to leave the biggest part of the comb for Honeyguide!

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Wasichana hao walifunga maziwa, ndizi, viazi vitamu na maji. Walichukuwa Kamba za kufungia kuni pamoja na panga kali ya kukatia kuni. Halafu waliondoka kwenda msituni.

translation_en.text:
The girls packed milk, bananas,
sweet potatoes and water.
They took ropes for tying firewood
and a sharp machete for chopping
the wood.
Then they left for the forest.

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Atieno aliwaita wengine, “Angalia, hapa kuna meno ya Unyalego ya dhahabu. Hebu tuyachukuwe.” Apiyo aliwakumbusha, “Msisahau onyo la nyanya. Tusichukuwe chochote kutoka msituni ila kuni.”

translation_en.text:
Atieno called to the others, "Look,
here are Unyalego's golden teeth.
Let us take them."
Apiyo reminded them, "Don't forget
grandmother's warning. We must
not take anything from the forest
except firewood."

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0081_msitu-wa-nyoka.md p5; Text: Joseph Sanchez Nadimo; Illustration: Rob Owen; Translation: Brigid Simiyu

claims.locator: raw/asp/sw/0081_msitu-wa-nyoka.md p5; Text: Joseph Sanchez Nadimo; Illustration: Rob Owen; Translation: Brigid Simiyu

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Ajoh alisema, “Simwamini nyanya. Nadhani alisema tu hivyo kutuzuia kuchukuwa tunachotaka. Anatuonea wivu. Nitayachukuwa meno ya dhahabu.” Dada zake walikuwa na wasiwasi. “Ajoh, tulikuonya,” walisema. Ajoh hakujali.

translation_en.text:
Ajoh said, "I don't trust
grandmother. I think she said that
to stop us having what we want. I
want the golden teeth."
Her sisters were worried. "Ajoh, we
warned you," they said.
Ajoh did not care.

translation_en.text:
Apiyo started to sing with a clear
voice:
"Sio mimi, sio mimi aliye na meno,
Mwenye meno bado yuko nyuma."
Then Atieno sang the song. She also
sang well.

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Graca alipewa kazi yakuhakikisha watoto wote walipata elimu nzuri.Ilikuwa kazi ngumu kwani watoto wengi wa Mozambigue hawakujua kusoma na kuandika.Alianza kwa kuwapeleka watoto wote shuleni.

translation_en.text:
Graça was given the important job
of making sure that all children in
Mozambique got a good education.
It was a hard job because there
were so many children in
Mozambique who couldn't read. She
knew that they needed education
and wanted to make real change in
her country. She started with
primary schools and getting boys
and girls into classrooms. Literacy
was her focus and putting books
into children's hands.

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0083_ndoto-ya-graca.md p9; Text: Melissa Fagan; Illustration: Karlien de Villiers; Translation: Rebbeccah Karoki

claims.locator: raw/asp/sw/0083_ndoto-ya-graca.md p9; Text: Melissa Fagan; Illustration: Karlien de Villiers; Translation: Rebbeccah Karoki

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Graca na Samora walijaliwa watoto wawili.Walikua na ndoto ya kuwapa watoto wao nawatu wa Mozambigue maisha mazuri.Siku moja Samora akafa kwa ajali ya ndege.

translation_en.text:
Graça and Samora had two
children. They shared a dream to
create good lives for their own
family and for the Mozambican
people. They were happy and
hopeful.
Then one terrible day, Samora died
in an aeroplane crash.

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0083_ndoto-ya-graca.md p10; Text: Melissa Fagan; Illustration: Karlien de Villiers; Translation: Rebbeccah Karoki

claims.locator: raw/asp/sw/0083_ndoto-ya-graca.md p10; Text: Melissa Fagan; Illustration: Karlien de Villiers; Translation: Rebbeccah Karoki

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Graca aliomboleza kifo cha Samora kwa miaka mingi.Baadaye Graca walipendana na Nelson Mandela na wakaona. walifanya kazi kwa pamoja kuwasaidia watoto wa Afrika.

translation_en.text:
Graça mourned Samora for many
years, but she found love again.
She met a man who had also spent
his life dreaming of bringing
freedom, hope and education to his
people.
Graça married Nelson Mandela and
together they worked to help
Africa's children.

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0083_ndoto-ya-graca.md p11; Text: Melissa Fagan; Illustration: Karlien de Villiers; Translation: Rebbeccah Karoki

claims.locator: raw/asp/sw/0083_ndoto-ya-graca.md p11; Text: Melissa Fagan; Illustration: Karlien de Villiers; Translation: Rebbeccah Karoki

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Plinyang' aliishi kwa familia hii na kuwa mkubw na alikuwa mwenye furaha. Alipendwa na alipenda kila mtu. Alipenda kupeleka wanyama malishoni na kuwachunga.

translation_en.text:
Palinyang' grew up in this family
and was very happy.
He was loved and he loved
everybody.
He enjoyed grazing the animals in
the fields.

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0088_kijana-palinyang.md p4; Text: Gaspah Emukuru Juma; Illustration: Wiehan de Jager; Translation: Carol Nangila

claims.locator: raw/asp/sw/0088_kijana-palinyang.md p4; Text: Gaspah Emukuru Juma; Illustration: Wiehan de Jager; Translation: Carol Nangila

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Palinyang' alimpenda ng'ombe mmoja sana hata kumpa jina Alinyang'. Alinyang' alikuwa ngo'mbe mzee katika mifugo wote. Kwa sababu hiyo mwenye mifugo alimthamini sana ngo'mbe huyo.

translation_en.text:
Palinyang' loved one particular cow
so much that he gave it the name
Alinyang'.
Alinyang' was the oldest cow in the
whole herd. For this reason, the
owner valued it a lot.

translation_en.text: At school, Khalai talks to the tree in the middle of the compound. "Please tree, put out big branches so we can read under your shade."

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Sungura alimwonea Kima wivu kwa kuwa na mkia mrefu. Alikuwa amezungumza na wenye shamba. "Kima atakuja kula mahindi yenu leo. Mfunze adabu!"

translation_en.text:
As Adun and the man journeyed
to his place, the owner of the
legs took the legs back.
Then the owner of the arms
took his arms back.
And finally the owner of the
body took that back.

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Walipokuwa wakila mahindi, Sungura alijificha na kupiga kelele akisema, "Mwizi! Mwizi! Mahindi yenu yanaliwa yote!" Kisha akatoroka na kwenda zake. Kima hakujua lililokuwa likiendelea.

translation_en.text:
Only the head was left, and the
head went on. Adun was scared
but she did not run away. They
arrived at the house of the
head.

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Hata hivyo, wenyewe hawakumsikiza. Mmoja alitoa panga na kusema, "Leo ni leo! Utashika adabu!" Aliukata mkia wake. Sungura alishuhudia kila kitu kutoka alikojificha.

translation_en.text:
Eventually Adun consulted a
diviner about what to do. The
diviner advised, "Go and buy
some bean cakes. Soak them in
palm oil and put them in
Tortoise's horn."

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0091_kima-apoteza-mkia-wake.md p10; Text: Mozambican folktale; Illustration: Horácio José Cossa, Onesmus Kakungi

claims.locator: raw/asp/sw/0091_kima-apoteza-mkia-wake.md p10; Text: Mozambican folktale; Illustration: Horácio José Cossa, Onesmus Kakungi

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Wenye shamba waliondoka na kwenda zao. Kima alipokimbilia usalama wake, Sungura aliuchukuwa mkia wa Kima na kwenda kuupika. "Nitamwalika Kima kwa chakula cha mchana," alitabasamu.

translation_en.text:
Adun followed the diviner's
instructions. She put the oily
cakes into the horn.

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0091_kima-apoteza-mkia-wake.md p11; Text: Mozambican folktale; Illustration: Horácio José Cossa, Onesmus Kakungi

claims.locator: raw/asp/sw/0091_kima-apoteza-mkia-wake.md p11; Text: Mozambican folktale; Illustration: Horácio José Cossa, Onesmus Kakungi

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Baada ya mlo, Kima alisema, "Asante rafiki yangu kwa kuandaa chakula kitamu." Sungura alimwuliza Kima ikiwa alijua alichokula. Bila kujua, Kima alijibu,"La, sijui!"

translation_en.text:
The following day, she took her
things and began to run away
again. When Tortoise took the
horn to blow it, the delicious
bean cakes fell into his mouth.

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0091_kima-apoteza-mkia-wake.md p12; Text: Mozambican folktale; Illustration: Horácio José Cossa, Onesmus Kakungi

claims.locator: raw/asp/sw/0091_kima-apoteza-mkia-wake.md p12; Text: Mozambican folktale; Illustration: Horácio José Cossa, Onesmus Kakungi

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Hata wapinzani hao wawili walisalia kuwa marafiki. Kobe hakujivuna kwa sababu ya ushindi wake, na sungura, akifahamu kuwa alikuwa ameshindwa kwa uwazi, hakumshikia kobe kisasi.

translation_en.text: Even the two competitors remained friends. The tortoise did not assume airs because he had won, and the hare, realising he had been defeated fair and square, bore the tortoise no grudge.

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0092_sungura-na-kobe-tena.md p3; Text: Venkatramana Gowda, Divaspathy Hegde; Illustration: Padmanabha; Translation: Brigid Simiyu

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Barabara ya kwenda kwa ufalme jirani haikuwa laini wala rahisi. Ilikuwa ya mawe na iliyojaa miiba. Vile vile kulikuwa na mito miwili njiani.

translation_en.text:
The road to the neighbouring kingdom was not smooth or easy.

It was rocky and full of thorns.

There were also two rivers to cross on the way.

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0092_sungura-na-kobe-tena.md p7; Text: Venkatramana Gowda, Divaspathy Hegde; Illustration: Padmanabha; Translation: Brigid Simiyu

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Baada ya kuwaza kiasi, sungura na kobe waligundua kwamba hakuna mmoja wao ambaye angeweza kutimiza ile kazi pekee yake. Walilazimika kusafiri kwa pamoja.

translation_en.text:
After some thought, both the hare and the tortoise realised that neither of them could complete the task alone.

They had to travel together.

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0092_sungura-na-kobe-tena.md p8; Text: Venkatramana Gowda, Divaspathy Hegde; Illustration: Padmanabha; Translation: Brigid Simiyu

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Kobe aliogelea kutoka upande mmoja wa mto hadi mwingine kwa wepesi. Baada ya kuvuka mito yote miwili, haikuwachukuwa muda mrefu kufika katika ule ufalme jirani.

translation_en.text:
The tortoise swam across the river gracefully.

Once both rivers had been crossed, it did not take them long to arrive at the neighbouring kingdom.

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0092_sungura-na-kobe-tena.md p12; Text: Venkatramana Gowda, Divaspathy Hegde; Illustration: Padmanabha; Translation: Brigid Simiyu

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Baada ya majadiliano mapana na yule mfalme jirani kuhusiana na mambo yote kutoka kwa mfalme wao, sungura na kobe walikuwa tayari kuondoka.

translation_en.text: After long discussions with the neighbouring king on all the matters raised by their own king, the hare and the tortoise were ready to leave.

items.text: Siku iliyofuata, Anansi alimaka asubuhi na mapema akamwamsha mamba mmoja. “Ningependa kwenda nimlete mke na watoto wangu ili wanisaidie kuhadithia. Je, utanisaidia niende kuwaleta kabla ya wengine kuamka?”

translation_en.text:
Early the next morning, before first
light, Anansi woke up one of the
crocodiles.
"I want to go and fetch my wife and
children from across the river, so
that they can help me tell my story.
Will you help me before the others
wake up?" he asked the crocodile.

items.text: Katika kijiji kimoja kwenye mteremko wa Mlima wa Kenya, katika Afrika Mashariki, msichana mdogo alifanya kazi za shambani pamoja na mama yake. Msichana huyu aliitwa Wangari.

translation_en.text: In a village on the slopes of Mount Kenya in East Africa, a little girl worked in the fields with her mother. Her name was Wangari.

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0110_mbegu-ndogo-hadithi-ya-wangari-maathai.md p1; Text: Nicola Rijsdijk; Illustration: Maya Marshak; Translation: Ursula Nafula

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Wangari alipenda kufanya kazi za nje. Alitumia jembe kulima katika bustani ya familia yake. Kisha alipanda mbegu ndogo katika ardhi yenye virutubisho.

translation_en.text: Wangari loved being outside. In her family's food garden she broke up the soil with her machete. She pressed tiny seeds into the warm earth.

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0110_mbegu-ndogo-hadithi-ya-wangari-maathai.md p2; Text: Nicola Rijsdijk; Illustration: Maya Marshak; Translation: Ursula Nafula

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Jinsi alivyojifunza ndivyo alivyofahamu kuwa aliwapenda watu wa Kenya. Alitaka wafurahi na wawe wenye uhuru. Jinsi alivyojifunza ndivyo alikumbuka kwao nyumbani Afrika.

translation_en.text:
The more she learnt, the more she realised that she loved the people of Kenya. She wanted them to be happy and free.

The more she learnt, the more she remembered her African home.

translation_en.text: As time passed, the new trees grew into forests, and the rivers started flowing again. Wangari's message spread across Africa. Today, millions of trees have grown from Wangari's seeds.

translation_en.text:
When the party started heating
up, the wax began to melt and
his horns fell off.
The horned animals were
shocked. "Who's that one with
no horns? Why did he come
here?" they asked.

translation_en.text:
The pain of losing her babies
made Monkey jump up and
down.
She would jump to one branch,
then to another, and cry out,
"Kwi! Kwi! Kwi!"

branch and put the baby on the
path.
At that time, a hunter was
returning home.
He saw the baby monkey lying
on the side of the path.

"Throw it up!
Throw it down!
Throw it to me!
Throw it to him!"
The baby monkey was thrown
from one child to the other.

items.text: Siku moja dada hao waliamka na kugundua kwamba hawakuwa na chochote cha kula. Walilazimika kutafuta chakula. Kwa hivyo Nelima na Nambuya walikwenda kila mmoja upande tofauti.

translation_en.text:
One day, the two sisters woke
up in the morning and found
that they had nothing to eat.
They had to look for food. So
Nelima and Nambuya went off
in different directions.

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Wakati huo huo, paliishi mwanamke mkongwe kwa jina Netasile. Aliaminiwa kupeana utajiri. Netasile alikuwa na ugonjwa wa ukoma na mwili wake ulijaa vidonda.

translation_en.text:
Meanwhile, there lived an old
woman called Netasile. She was
believed to be a giver of riches.
Netasile had leprosy and her
body was full of sores.

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Nambuya alitembea hadi akafika mahali walipokuwa jongoo, nyoka, mabuu na wadudu wengine. Alikuwa amechoka na kudhoofika kwa kukosa chakula. Alipoketi chini kupmzika, wadudu hawa walianza kumuuma.

translation_en.text:
Nambuya walked until she
reached a strange place. A
place where there were
millipedes, snakes, caterpillars
and many other insects.
Nambuya was very tired and
weak because she had not
eaten anything. When she sat
down to rest, these creatures
preyed on her.

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Njiani, Nelima alimkuta mwanamke yule yule. Alifurahi kumwona Netasile kwani alikuwa binadamu wa kwanza kukutana naye tangu aanze safari yake. Mwanamke alimwita na kumuuliza maswali yale yale.

translation_en.text:
On her journey, Nelima came to
the same woman. She was
happy to see Netasile, being
the first person she met since
starting her journey. The old
woman called her and asked
the same questions.

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0166_msichana-aliyetajirika.md p9; Text: Salaama Wanale; Illustration: Mango Tree; Translation: Brigid Simiyu

items.text: Nelima alikubali kumpeleka nyumbani kwake. “Umefanya kile wengi wemekosa kufanya," mwanamke alisema. Alimpa Nelima kijiti na kumwambia arudi nyumbani ambako angekuta kila kitu alichotaka.

translation_en.text:
Nelima agreed to carry Netasile
to her house. "You have done
what many have failed to do,"
said the old woman. She gave
Nelima a stick and told her to
go back home, where she would
find everything she wanted.

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0166_msichana-aliyetajirika.md p10; Text: Salaama Wanale; Illustration: Mango Tree; Translation: Brigid Simiyu

translation_en.text:
Nelima was very grateful and
thanked the old woman and ran
back home. She found a new
house with everything in it, and
a lot of food. She became the
richest woman in the land.

translation_en.text:
Long, long ago there were seven
suns in the sky.
Their rays made the earth so hot
that human beings could not bear
it.

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: “Nitaliita jua lirudi,” simba alisema. Yeye alikuwa mfalme wa msitu huo. “Jua, jua, tafadhali usitutoroke. Rudi tena utuangazie,” simba alinguruma. Lakini jua lilikataa kusikiliza.

translation_en.text:
"I will call out to the sun," said the
lion, for he was the king of the
forest.
"Sun, sun, please do not run away
from us. Come back in and shine on
us," roared the lion.
But the sun did not listen to him.

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0167_jua-la-saba.md p6; Text: Indian Folktale; Illustration: Pratham Books; Translation: Kamundi Mutugi

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Jogoo alisimama mbele ya wanyama wote, na taratibu akawika, “kookoodookoo-koo.” Jua lilianza kuchomoza kutoka nyuma ya mlima. Wanyama wote walishangaa kuona haya.

translation_en.text:
The rooster stepped forward and
gently crowed, "Kookoodokoo koo."
To everyone's surprise, the sun
peeped out a little from behind the
hill.

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0167_jua-la-saba.md p9; Text: Indian Folktale; Illustration: Pratham Books; Translation: Kamundi Mutugi

claims.locator: raw/asp/sw/0167_jua-la-saba.md p9; Text: Indian Folktale; Illustration: Pratham Books; Translation: Kamundi Mutugi

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Wanyama waliwaagiza binadamu wasiliue jua. Tangu siku hiyo, jogoo huwika kila asubuhi. Nalo jua lisikiapo sauti ya jogoo, huchomoka na kuangaza duniani.

translation_en.text:
The animals asked the human
beings not to kill the sun and they
agreed.
Ever since that day, when the
rooster crows in the morning, the
sun rises and shines in the sky.

items.text: Anansi alifanya hivyo. Kisha akamfunga yule nyoka kwenye kijiti kile kwa kutumia kamba ili kumnyoosha sawasawa. Baada ya kumfunga huyo nyoka vizuri, alimbeba hadi juu mbinguni.

translation_en.text:
So Anansi did that, and he tied the
snake to the stick with his vine to
keep him straight.
When he was all tied up, Anansi
took the snake up to heaven.

items.text: Fisi na kunguru walikuwa marafiki sana hapo awali ingawaje tabia zao zilikuwa tofauti sana kwa njia nyingine. Kunguru aliweza kuruka lakini fisi hakuweza isipokuwa kutembea tu.

translation_en.text:
Hyena and Raven were once great
friends, even though they were
quite different in some ways.
Raven could fly but Hyena was only
able to walk.

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0170_fisi-na-kunguru.md p1; Text: Ann Nduku; Illustration: Wiehan de Jager; Translation: Pete Mhunzi

claims.locator: raw/asp/sw/0170_fisi-na-kunguru.md p1; Text: Ann Nduku; Illustration: Wiehan de Jager; Translation: Pete Mhunzi

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Kunguru kwa ukarimu wake alimpa fisi manyoya. Fisi aliyashona yawe mbawa. Akayaunganisha na mwili wake akajaribu kuruka. Lakini uzito wake ulimshinda. Sasa ilibidi afikirie mpango mpya.

translation_en.text:
Raven was not mean, so he gave
him some feathers.
Hyena sewed them together into
wings. He fastened them to his
body, and tried to take off into the
sky.
But he was far too heavy for the
few feathers to carry him.
So he had to think of another plan.

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0170_fisi-na-kunguru.md p3; Text: Ann Nduku; Illustration: Wiehan de Jager; Translation: Pete Mhunzi

claims.locator: raw/asp/sw/0170_fisi-na-kunguru.md p3; Text: Ann Nduku; Illustration: Wiehan de Jager; Translation: Pete Mhunzi

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Fisi alikuwa akitamani nyama iliyokuwa juu mbele kidogo akatokwa na udenda tena. Kunguru aliruka na kuruka mpaka akachoka kabisa. Lakini fisi akamwomba, “endelea kidogo tu rafiki yangu!”

translation_en.text:
Raven flew and flew and flew until
he was exhausted. But Hyena said,
"Just a little further, my friend!"
He could see the white and fatty
meat just above them, and his
mouth was watering.

items.text: Sungura alishinda mbio zote. Ndovu alikasirika kwa sababu hakuwahi kushindwa. Kwa hivyo alimuuliza Sungura, “Nini kinachokuwezesha kuwa mkimbiaji maarufu?” Sungura alijibu, “Miguu yangu myembamba.”

translation_en.text:
Hare won all the races.
Elephant was upset
because he had never
been defeated.
So he asked Hare,
"What makes you a
good runner?"
Hare answered,
"My thin legs."

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0183_sungura-na-ndovu-tena.md p7; Text: Agnes Gachaba; Illustration: Wiehan de Jager

claims.locator: raw/asp/sw/0183_sungura-na-ndovu-tena.md p7; Text: Agnes Gachaba; Illustration: Wiehan de Jager

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Bila kuwaza zaidi, Ndovu aliuliza kile angelifanya ili miguu yake iwe myembamba. Sungura alisema, “Ni rahisi, nitakuonyesha. Tafuta kuni na ukoke moto.”

translation_en.text:
Without a second thought,
Elephant asked what
he could do to make
his legs thin.
Hare said, "It is simple,
I will show you with fire."

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0183_sungura-na-ndovu-tena.md p8; Text: Agnes Gachaba; Illustration: Wiehan de Jager

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Ndovu alikusanya kuni na kukoka moto mkubwa. Sungura alisema, “Sasa iweke miguu yako motoni.” Ndovu alisimama ndani ya moto. Alipiga kelele, “Nateketea! Nateketea!”

translation_en.text:
Hare said, "Put your legs
in the fire."
Elephant stepped into
the fire. He shouted,
"I am burning! I am
burning!"

items.text: Palikuwa na msichana kwa jina Mulongo. Aliishi na wazazi wake karibu na kijiji cha Budongo. Siku moja mamake Mulongo alimtuma kuchota maji kisimani.

translation_en.text:
There was once a girl called
Mulongo who lived with her
parents near the village of
Budongo.
One day Mulongo's mother sent
her to fetch water at the well.

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0184_mulongo-na-fisi.md p1; Text: Sarah Nangobi; Illustration: Wiehan de Jager; Translation: Brigid Simiyu

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Alifuata njia iliyoelekea kwenye kijito. Upande mwingine wa kijito kulikuwa na njia nyingine ndogo kila mojawapo ikielekea upande tofauti. “Njia ipi marafiki zake walifuata?” alishangaa.

translation_en.text:
She followed a path that led to
a stream.
On the other side of the stream
were many tiny paths each one,
leading in a different direction.
"Which path had her friends
taken?" she wondered.

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0184_mulongo-na-fisi.md p4; Text: Sarah Nangobi; Illustration: Wiehan de Jager; Translation: Brigid Simiyu

claims.locator: raw/asp/sw/0184_mulongo-na-fisi.md p4; Text: Sarah Nangobi; Illustration: Wiehan de Jager; Translation: Brigid Simiyu

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Aliichagua njia iliyokuwa pana kisha akatembea, na kutembea, lakini hakuwapata marafiki zake. Alichoka sana kwa hivyo alipopumzika chini ya mti, alilala mara moja.

translation_en.text:
She chose the biggest path, and
walked and walked, but she
could not find her friends.
She was so tired that when she
sat under a tree to rest, she fell
fast asleep.

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Mulongo alipoamka, ilikuwa giza. Gizani, macho ya manjano yalimulika. Alikuwa amezungukwa na fisi! Aliogopa asiweze hata kulia. Alijaribu kukimbia, lakini fisi walimzunguka wakionyesha wazi kuwa walikuwa na njaa.

translation_en.text:
When Mulongo woke up, it was
dark. In the darkness, yellow
eyes were gleaming. She was
surrounded by hyenas!
She was too terrified even to
cry out. She tried running, but
the hyenas circled her hungrily.

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0184_mulongo-na-fisi.md p6; Text: Sarah Nangobi; Illustration: Wiehan de Jager; Translation: Brigid Simiyu

claims.locator: raw/asp/sw/0184_mulongo-na-fisi.md p6; Text: Sarah Nangobi; Illustration: Wiehan de Jager; Translation: Brigid Simiyu

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Badala yake fisi walimpeleka Mulongo katika nyumba yao iliyokuwa ndani ya msitu. Chumba kilikuwa kichafu kilichojaa mifupa na kelele ya nzi. Alilala chini na kudanganya kuwa amelala usingizi.

translation_en.text:
But instead the hyenas took
Mulongo to their house in the
forest. It was a dirty hut full of
bones and buzzing flies.
She lay down and pretended to
go to sleep.

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0184_mulongo-na-fisi.md p8; Text: Sarah Nangobi; Illustration: Wiehan de Jager; Translation: Brigid Simiyu

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Walikuwa karibu kumvuta Mulongo kumtoa chumbani wakati fisi mkubwa aliongea, “Fisi, subirini. Kumbuka kanuni ya kijiji. Hakuna fisi anayekubaliwa kula pekee- ni lazima tuialike jamii nzima kushiriki mlo.”

translation_en.text:
But the big hyena spoke,
"Hyenas, wait. Remember the
rule of the village. No hyena
may eat alone. We have to
invite the whole family to share
a meal."
"I'll go and call the in-laws,"
said his wife.
"I'll go and fetch my cousins,"
said the small hyena.
"I'll fetch our brothers and
sisters," said another.
"And I will remain here with our
food," said the big hyena.

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0184_mulongo-na-fisi.md p10; Text: Sarah Nangobi; Illustration: Wiehan de Jager; Translation: Brigid Simiyu

claims.locator: raw/asp/sw/0184_mulongo-na-fisi.md p10; Text: Sarah Nangobi; Illustration: Wiehan de Jager; Translation: Brigid Simiyu

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Njia ilikuwa ni moja tu. Alijihimiza na kurukia juu ya mgongo wa fisi kwa mara moja, kisha akakimbia, na kukimbia jinsi miguu yake alivyomwezesha.

translation_en.text:
There was only one way.
She took a flying leap right over
the hyena's back, and ran as
fast as her legs could carry her.

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0184_mulongo-na-fisi.md p12; Text: Sarah Nangobi; Illustration: Wiehan de Jager; Translation: Brigid Simiyu

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Wakati huo huo, fisi wale wengine walirudi na kuona kilichotokea. Walimfuata huku wakipiga kelele za hasira na gadhabu. Lakini, walikuwa wamechelewa.

translation_en.text:
Just then the other hyenas
returned, and saw what had
happened. They ran after her,
howling with anger and
disappointment.
But it was too late.

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Hapo zamani za kale hapakuwa na usiku katika kijiji cha kina Opio. Watu walilala wakati wowote ule waliposikia uchovu. Walifanya kazi walipokuwa hawajalala.

translation_en.text:
Long ago, there was no night in
Opio's village.
People slept when they were tired
and worked when they were awake.

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0185_usiku-ulivyoingia-katika-kijiji-cha-kina-opio.md p1; Text: Robert Ekuka; Illustration: Wiehan de Jager; Translation: Mutugi Kamundi

claims.locator: raw/asp/sw/0185_usiku-ulivyoingia-katika-kijiji-cha-kina-opio.md p1; Text: Robert Ekuka; Illustration: Wiehan de Jager; Translation: Mutugi Kamundi

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Asubuhi iliyofuata, yule jamaa, alimweleza Opio, “Giza likianza kuingia leo tembea kwenda kijijini kwenu. Ukitembea huku ukiangalia mbele usiku utakufuata. Hupaswi kamwe kuangalia nyuma. Ukiangalia nyuma usiku utapotea.”

translation_en.text:
The next morning he asked his
friend,
"How can I take the night to my
own village? I want my people to
see the night."
"When it starts to get dark this
evening, walk to your village. If you
look straight in front, the night will
follow you. But you must not look
back. If you look back, the night will
go away."

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0185_usiku-ulivyoingia-katika-kijiji-cha-kina-opio.md p6; Text: Robert Ekuka; Illustration: Wiehan de Jager; Translation: Mutugi Kamundi

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Opio alifanya alivyoambiwa. Usiku huo alianza kutembea akielekea kijijini kwao. Alisikia giza la usiku likimfuata nyuma yake. Alitaka kuangalia nyuma lakini hakuangalia.

translation_en.text:
Opio did as he was told. That
evening, he began to walk towards
his village.
He felt the dark night behind him as
he walked.
He wanted to look back.
But he did not.

translation_en.text: One day, Hare was out looking for food. He met Elephant, who had a pot of honey. Hare asked Elephant, "Please be kind and carry me. I am weak."

translation_en.text:
These animals ate all their
crops and even carried children
away.
It was not a good place to live
any longer, but where could the
people go?

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Vichaka vilimea katikati mwa pengo za miamba. Miti ilimea kwenye mitelemko ya milima. Wazazi walitega sungura wa miambani. Watoto walishika ndege.

translation_en.text:
Bushes grew in the cracks
between rocks.
Trees grew on the slopes of the
hills.
The parents trapped rock
rabbits and the children caught
birds.

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Familia zingine ziliona jinsi familia ya milimani ilivyoishi vizuri. “Maisha ya kule milimani ni mazuri,” bwana alisema. “Lazima mje huko pia.”

translation_en.text:
Other families noticed how well
the hill family lived.
"It is a good life up in the hills,"
said the husband. "You should
come there too."

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Polepole, vitu vilianza kubadilika. Watoto walipunguza kuongea, na kukoroma zaidi. Kisha watu wazima waliona kwamba pua zao zilikuwa zinakuwa kubwa. Waliota nywele zaidi.

translation_en.text:
Slowly, things began to change.
The children talked less, and
grunted more. Then the adults
noticed that their noses were
getting bigger and that they
were growing more hair.

translation_en.text:
Shy but brave, the little girl moved nearer to the woman.

"We must keep her with us," the little girl's people decided. "We'll keep her and her child safe."

translation_en.text:
And so the woman found herself alone again.

She wondered what to do with this awkward child.

She wondered what to do with herself.

items.text: Wakati aliposimama, ilikuwa ni usiku, na alikuwa amepotea. "Hee haw?" alinong'ona gizani. "Hee haw?" giza likatoa mwangwi. Alikuwa mwenyewe. Alijikunyata katika umbo dogo, akalala fofofo usingizi wa mang'amung'amu.

translation_en.text:
By the time he stopped running, it was night, and Donkey was lost.

"Hee haw?" he whispered to the darkness.

"Hee Haw?" it echoed back. He was alone.

Curling himself into a tight ball, he fell into a deep and troubled sleep.

translation_en.text:
Donkey went to stay with the old man, who taught him many different ways to survive.

Donkey listened and learned, and so did the old man. They helped each other, and they laughed together.

items.text: Refiloe alimweka kuku wa kwanza ndani ya ndoo ya maji. “Kaa wima, ewe kiumbe shenzi,” Refiloe alipiga kelele. “Haitachukuwa muda mrefu!”

translation_en.text:
Refiloe put the first chicken into the
bucket of water.
It clucked at the top of its voice and
flapped its wings like crazy.
"Hold still you silly thing," Refiloe
shouted, "this won't take long!"
When Refiloe wiped the chicken's
nose and eyes it suddenly went
limp and
flopped over the side of the bucket.

items.text: Shangazi zake Refiloe, yaani Mama Ngwe na Mama Pedi, walikuwa wakitayarisha harusi ya Palesa kwa muda mrefu. Walitakiwa wafanye matayarisho hayo kwa pamoja lakini hawakupendana hata kidogo.

translation_en.text:
Mme Ngwe and Mme Pedi were
Refiloe's aunts. They did not like
each other at all.
The aunts had been preparing for
months for Palesa's wedding, but
they would not even think about
riding together in the same taxi.

Rooster decided to play a joke
on Hare.
He said, "My friend, we birds
have a secret for going to sleep.
At bedtime, we chop off our
heads. Without heads, we sleep
very well."

translation_en.text:
Her grandmother spent many hours
making a handsome makgabe for
Tasneem. Tasneem loved to wear
that apron.

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0218_nyanya-na-msichana-aliyenuka.md p2; Text: Southern African Folktale; Illustration: Catherine Groenewald; Translation: Brigid Simiyu

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Wasichana wengine wa pale kijijini walimwonea Tasneem wivu kwa ajili ya sketi yake. Waliona heri waiondoe. Lakini ni vigumu kuchukuwa nguo ya mtu ikiwa ameivaa.

translation_en.text:
The other girls in that place were
jealous of Tasneem's makgabe.
They thought that it would be better
to get rid of it.
But it is a difficult thing to take a
person's clothes when that person
is wearing them.

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Tasneem alikumbuka jinsi alivyonuka vibaya. Alikumbuka jinsi walivyomchukulia. Aliwaambia kwamba hangewahi kwenda katika nyumba yao tena. “Lazima wazazi wawapende watoto wao,” alisema, “hata kama watoto wao wananuka vibaya.”

translation_en.text:
Tasneem remembered how she had
smelled so bad.
She told them that she would never
go back to their house.
"Parents must love their children,"
she said, "even if their children
smell very bad."

translation_en.text:

The villagers prepared food and animals to be slaughtered.

translation_en.text:
Early the next morning, they left for the village in their father's car.

They drove past mountains, wild animals and tea plantations. They counted cars and sang songs.

translation_en.text: Odongo and Apiyo helped their grandmother with household chores. They fetched water and firewood. They collected eggs from the chickens and picked greens from the garden.

items.text: Nyar-Kanyada aliwafundisha wajukuu wake jinsi ya kupika ugali mwepesi wa kula na mchuzi. Aliwaonesha namna ya kupika wali wa nazi wa kuliwa na samaki wa kukaanga.

translation_en.text: Nyar-Kanyada taught her grandchildren to make soft ugali to eat with stew. She showed them how to make coconut rice to eat with roast fish.

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Baba yao alipokuja kuwachukua, hawakutaka kuondoka. Walimuomba Nyar-Kanyada aende nao mjini. Alitabasamu na kusema, "Nimezeeka, siyawezi ya mjini. Nitasubiri mje kijijini kwangu tena."

translation_en.text:
When their father came to fetch them, they did not want to leave. The children begged Nyar-Kanyada to go with them to the city.

She smiled and said, "I am too old for the city. I will be waiting for you to come to my village again."

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Mtu yule aliposikia hivyo, alikimbia nyumbani kwa kasi kama risasi... Alimpata mkewe tayari akiwa amefariki. Alihuzunika sana kwa ajili ya yale alikuwa amefanya. Naye alitaka kufa.

translation_en.text:
When the man heard that, he
ran home as fast as a bullet ...
Only to find his wife had just
died.
He was so grief stricken
because of what he had done
that he too died.

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: “Unaenda wapi?” Yule msichana alimwuliza. “Ninamtembelea mjombangu Mtonyama,” Nonkungu alisema. “Ala! Mtonyama ni mjombangu pia nami namtembelea,” yule msichana akasema. Wakatembea pamoja.

translation_en.text:
"Where are you going?" asked the
young girl.
"I'm going to visit my Uncle
Mtonyama," said Nonkungu.
"Well, Mtonyama is my uncle, too
and I am also on my way to visit
him," said the young girl.
So they walked on together.

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0251_nonkungu-na-imbulu.md p4; Text: Alan Kenyon, Viv Kenyon; Illustration: Wiehan de Jager; Translation: Mutugi Kamundi

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Nduguye Mtonyama alitembea shambani na kusikia wimbo mtamu. Alirudi nyumbani akamweleza Mtonyama. Mtonyama alienda kuusikiliza akamwona Nonkungu.

translation_en.text:
One day, one of Mtonyama's
brothers was walking in the fields.
He heard the strange and beautiful
song.
He didn't know who was singing,
but when he got home, he told
Mtonyama the words.
Mtonyama went into the fields. He
heard the song, and looked until he
found Nonkungu.

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0251_nonkungu-na-imbulu.md p13; Text: Alan Kenyon, Viv Kenyon; Illustration: Wiehan de Jager; Translation: Mutugi Kamundi

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Mtonyama alisikia kwamba mkia wa Imbulu ulipenda kunywa maziwa. Wafanyi kazi wake walichimba shimo wakalijaza maziwa. Wasichana wote kijijini walishindana kuruka.

translation_en.text:
Mtonyama had heard that an
imbulu's tail loves milk and that it
can't go past milk without drinking
some.
So he told his men to dig a deep
ditch and to fill the ditch with sour
milk.
Then he called all the girls of the
village to take part in a jumping
competition.

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0251_nonkungu-na-imbulu.md p15; Text: Alan Kenyon, Viv Kenyon; Illustration: Wiehan de Jager; Translation: Mutugi Kamundi

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Imbulu alipokuwa akitapatapa ndani ya maziwa, wanaume waliliziba lile shimo na kumzika. Nonkungu aliishi na mjombake kwa furaha kwa miaka mingi. Na huo ndio mwisho wa hadithi.

translation_en.text:
As the imbulu struggled in the sour
milk, the men quickly filled the
ditch with sand and buried her. That
was the end of the imbulu.
Nonkungu stayed happily with her
uncle for a long, long time.
And that is the end of the story.

translation_en.text:
Grandmother is silent.
Selma touches the smooth skin of
the baobab.
"So it was the tree that saved them
all," she says.

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Mamangu alinifariji kwa kusema, “Utakuwa na jozi nyingi baadaye, subiri tu utaona!” Wakati mwingine sikumwamini. “Baadaye itakuwa lini?” Nilimwuliza siku moja.

translation_en.text:
My mother would say, "You will
have many pairs in the future,
just wait!"
Sometimes I did not believe her.
"When is the future?" I asked
her one day.

items.text: Kisha ulikuwa msimu wa Krismasi. Kila mtu alijishughulisha kwenda sokoni na kurejea na vitu vipya. “Je, mama, nasi tutaenda sokoni?” Nilimwuliza.

translation_en.text:
Time passed and it was nearly
Christmas.
Everybody was busy going to
the market and coming back
with bags of new things.
"Mother, are we going to the
market?" I asked her.

translation_en.text:
We went straight to where there
were many different types of

My eyes were wide with

after row of neatly arranged
shoes.

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Muda mfupi baadaye, niliamka kitandani na kuvijaribu tena viatu vyangu. Nilitembea pole pole chumbani kisha nikavirejesha ndani ya sanduku. Nililala lakini sikupata usingizi.

translation_en.text:
After a while, I got out of bed
and put on the shoes.
I walked slowly around the room
and then put the shoes back
into
the box.
I lay down again, but I couldn't
sleep.

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0256_viatu-vyangu-vya-kwanza.md p8; Text: Ursula Nafula; Illustration: Rob Owen

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Nililala mara nyingine nikinuia kupata usingizi. Lakini muda mfupi baadaye, niliamka kwa mara ya tatu. Nilivivaa vyatu nikaruka ruka chumbani kidogo. Nilihisi usingizi nikarudi kitandani.

translation_en.text:
I lay down once more and tried
to sleep. But I got up a third
time.
I put on the shoes and jumped
around the room. Then I felt
tired.
I decided to get back into bed.

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Hapo zamani za kale, palikuwa na mvulana aliyekuwa na sura mbaya sana. Hakupendwa na yeyote, hata wazazi wake. Akiwa nyumbani, aliketi peke yake wakati familia yake iliangalia runinga.

translation_en.text:
Once upon a time, there was a boy
who was so ugly that nobody loved
him, even his parents.
At home, he would sit alone while
his family watched television.

sources.locator: raw/asp/sw/0260_mvulana-asiyependwa-na-yeyote.md p1; Text: Phumy Zikode; Illustration: Wiehan de Jager; Translation: Brigid Simiyu

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Siku moja aliamua kuondoka, lakini hakujua pa kwenda. Alitembea hadi akaufikia msitu asili. Alianza kuogopa. Lakini aliwaza kuwa hakuna angetaka kuzungumza naye kwani hakuna aliyempenda.

translation_en.text:
One day he decided to leave, but he
didn't know where he would go. He
walked until he got to an indigenous
forest. He started to get scared but
was comforted by the thought that
nobody would speak to him
because nobody loved him.

translation_en.text: He shared his fears with Thomas. Over time the man reassured the boy that life could be better at the new place.

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Magozwe alianza kwenda shule na haikuwa rahisi. Mara nyingi alitaka kukata tamaa. Lakini alipofikiria juu ya rubani na mchezaji kandanda maarufu aliosoma katika vitabu vya hadithi, alivumilia.

translation_en.text:
Magozwe started school and it was difficult. He had a lot to catch up. Sometimes he wanted to give up.

But he thought about the pilot and the soccer player in the storybooks. Like them, he did not give up.

items.label: beta

can_do: C1.READ: Understand authentic sentences of level C1
items.text: Wanyama walifurahi waliposikia kwamba wangepewa miguu. Kila mnyama alitaka miguu ili aweze kutembea na kukimbia. Waliimba, wakachezesha mikia yao na kupapata mbawa zao.

translation_en.text:
The animals were happy when they heard that they would be given legs.

Each animal wanted to have legs so that it could walk and run.

They sang, wagged their tails and flapped their wings.

items.text: Wanyama walikusanyika na kujadili jinsi ilivyokuwa vigumu kutambaa ardhini. Ardhi ilikwaruza tumbo zao. Miguu itawasaidia kusimama na kuona mbali, kama vile binadamu walivyokuwa.

translation_en.text:
Animals gathered and discussed how difficult it was to crawl.

The ground scratched their bellies.

Legs would also help them to stand and see far, like human beings did.

items.text: Siku ilipofika, wanyama wengi walitambaa na kufika nyumbani kwa Maguru ili wapate miguu. Twiga, simba, ndovu, sungura, mamba, na ndege, wote walipanga foleni wakisubiri kupewa miguu.

translation_en.text:
When the day came, many animals crawled to Maguru's house to get their legs.

Giraffes, lions, elephants, rabbits, crocodiles, and birds queued and waited to be given legs.

items.text: Mnyama wa mwisho kwenye foleni alikuwa Jongoo. Maguru aliuliza, “Je, kuna yeyote baada ya wewe?” “La! Mimi ni wa mwisho,” Jongoo alijibu.

translation_en.text:
The last animal in the queue was the millipede.

Maguru asked, "Is there anyone else after you?"

"No, I am the last one," Millipede answered.

translation_en.text:
Anansi happily headed home with
his basket on his head, singing.
He was thinking about all the things
he was going to buy with his money.

items.text: Waliwaita tena Anansi na Tai. “Tunaamini usemi wa Tai,” walisema. “Yeye si mwizi. Ulikuwa ukijitakia kitu kisichokuwa chako.” Anansi, Buibui hakuweza kuamini masikio yake. Aliangua kilio.

translation_en.text:
They summoned Anansi and the
Vulture again.
"We believe Vulture's story," they
said. "He is not the thief. You were
trying to claim something that was
not yours."
Anansi could not believe his ears!
He burst into tears.

items.text: Sasa akaanza kazi ya kumchonga mke kutoka kwa gogo la mti. Wakati alikuwa amemaliza kuchonga sanamu, aliigusa macho ikaanza kuona. Kisha aliipulizia pumzi ikawa hai.

translation_en.text:
So he set to work to shape a
beautiful woman from a strong
branch of the tree. When he had
finished making the statue, he
touched her eyes, and they opened.
He blew gently on her, and she
came alive.

items.text: Lakini kabla ya kipindi kirefu, vijana kutoka kijiji jirani walianza kusema, “Inawezekanaje mzee kama huyu kumwoa msichana mrembo namna hii!” Basi wakaamua kumwiba msichana yule wampeleke kijijini kwao.

translation_en.text:
But before long, the young men
from a neighbouring village began
talking among themselves.
"How can such an old man have
such a beautiful young wife?"
So they decided to steal her and
take her to their own kraal.

translation_en.text:
When they found her, they sang to
her in the language of birds:
Tree woman, tree woman
More beautiful than any other
Your husband has sent us
To bring back your apron!

A little later they passed Sparrow.

"Yes, Sparrow, I'm looking for my house. Have you seen it, by any chance?"
Sparrow said: "No, I haven't, but I'll help you look!"

He flapped his wings and he
whizzed away.
"But you're going too fast for
me," complained
Tortoise.
Sparrow came back. "Alright,
then I'll hop on too."

translation_en.text:
Tortoise carried on, with Snail
and Sparrow perched
on his shell. They looked and
looked, but there was
no sign of a house. The sun had
inched lower in the
sky.

translation_en.text:
A little later they passed Mouse. He was making a garland of daisies.
"Are you looking for something?" asked Mouse.
"Yes, Mouse, I'm looking for my house. Have you seen it, by any chance?"

stretched and stretched and
scooped up his daisies.

items.text: Alikuwa mvulana NA msichana – mapacha! Mvulana alimwita Mukhwana, na msichana akamwita Mulongo. Alipomwangalia Mukhwana, alifurahi sana. Lakini alipomwangalia Mulongo, alihuzunika mno. Ni jambo moja tu angelifanya.

translation_en.text:
It was a boy AND a girl – twins!
She called the boy Mukhwana,
and the girl she called Mulongo.
As she looked at Mukhwana,
she was very happy. But as she
looked at Mulongo, she felt sad.
She felt that there was only one
thing she could do.

items.text: Hii ilifanyika tena na tena. Mukhwana hakujua la kufanya. Kwa hivyo alimwendea mamake, Namukhaywa. “Nimempata msichana mrembo,” alisema. “Nataka kumuoa. Lakini kila ninapomuuliza, anaimba wimbo ule ule.”

translation_en.text:
This happened again and again.
Mukhwana did not know what
to do. So he went to his mother,
Namukhaywa.
"I have found a beautiful girl,"
he said. "And I want to marry
her. But every time I ask her,
she sings the same song."

the story, he saw that he had
been wrong. He called
Namukhaywa and together they
went to the midwife to fetch

Sakima learned that the rich man's son was missing.

The man was very sad and lonely.

translation_en.text:
"I can sing for him. He might be happy again," Sakima told his parents.

But his parents dismissed him.

"He is very rich. You are only a blind boy. Do you think your song will help him?"
